To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose Dis2Vec, a disease vocabulary driven model for disease surveillance.
Dis2Vec is able to capture taxonomical information from news articles and that this information can be used to augment traditional disease surveillance.

(a) Dis2Vec is an effective tool to model disease and constituent attributes as vectors in a low dimensional vector space, (b) these vectors can be used for taxonomical classification of diseases, and (c) Dis2Vec out performs state-of-the-art word2vec methods for disease classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel disease surveillance methods that are able to capture taxonomical and semantic attributes of diseases from unstructured text sources.
developing a disease representation that can capture the semantic and taxonomical structure of disease entities and their attributes.
augmenting existing surveillance systems with a vocabulary driven word2Vec approach that is capable of automatically generating disease taxonomies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model outperforms the state of the art in terms of accuracy, and is a promising approach for disease surveillance.
our proposed model is a significant improvement over traditional word2vec models for the task of disease taxonomy construction and can be used to augment existing surveillance tools.
our proposed model is capable of automatically learning taxonomical correlations between diseases from unstructured text.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Dis2Vec is a promising approach to model diseases from unstructured text and can be used to augment existing surveillance systems.
Dis2Vec is able to accurately capture the taxonomical attributes and relationships of diseases from unstructured news text.
, Dis2Vec can be used to augment traditional surveillance systems with a real-time and automated disease taxonomy generation tool.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dis2Vec can be used as a tool for disease surveillance by automatically generating disease taxonomies from unstructured text.
disease vocabulary driven word embeddings can help augment traditional surveillance tools by providing a more accurate representation of diseases and their constituent attributes.
disease taxonomies can be automatically constructed from unstructured news data, which can be leveraged to augment traditional surveillance systems with real-time disease data.
